newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended firmer on Monday in thin trade characterised by the absence of U.K. players in the market.
At the 1400 GMT finish, the rand was pegged at 4.5330/5380 against the dollar from 4.5400/5450 on Friday.
"It has been exceptionally quiet without the U.K. guys in," one trader said. U.K. markets were closed on Monday for a bank holiday.
"We've seen run-of-the-mill importer demand below the 4.54 level and there is a bit of exporter interest at the 4.5450 level," another dealer said.
A late inflow of dollars in after-hours trade helped the currency down to the 4.53 bid level, where it was quoted at 1417 GMT.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.0496/0605 on sterling from 7.0514/0614 on Friday and at 0.3258/3262 marks from 0.3272/3277 marks previously.
On the capital market, bonds attracted similar levels of interest in what was described by most traders as jobber-driven trade.
Initial concerns that the rise in the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond yield to a four-week closing high of 6.95 percent on Friday would weigh on the market, failed to materialise.
Government's key R150 was last pegged at 15.525 percent from 15.555 percent on Friday, while Eskom's 168 was at 15.67 percent from 15.69 percent previously.
Dealers said the markets were also generally on hold ahead of Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' annual address in Pretoria on Tuesday.
Although traders said they were expecting no surprises from the governor's speech, they were looking to Stals for "guidance and stability" following the market's recent gyrations.
"The market needs a clear signal on where interest rates are going," one trader said.

The release of second quarter GDP on Tuesday morning, followed July trade, money supply and private sector credit extension on data from Wednesday, were also expected to provide the market with some direction, dealers said.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 27.25 million rand of South African bonds on Friday after selling 77.09 million rand on Thursday. Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 7.49 billion rand from 4.39 billion rand.

On the money market, three-month NCDs eased to between 16.65 and 16.75 percent from 16.65 and 16.85 percent on Friday, while 90-day BAs were also lower at between 16.05 to 16.20 percent from 16.10 to 16.20 percent previously.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 8.157 billion rand on Saturday from 8.162 billion rand on Wednesday.
